diagnostic: Within each complete physical training factorial hold the current source, native probability of the first action and this window's native marginal use of the second activity skill fixed. Let the second skill depend arbitrarily on the observed first action. Optimize the two conditional probabilities within native log-odds +/-2, and independently over [0,1]. Measure how much F1 can be gained exclusively by moving suffix probability from one reached memory state to the other. Count windows with reversed nonzero preferred suffixes, identical memory vectors, and their question mass. Give each question equal weight within a panel. This is a hindsight upper bound for the specified reallocation and never a training target or promotion score.
population: Use all 12 early four-trajectory windows / 91 questions and, separately, each verified member of the 12 randomized donor windows / 88 questions when all four physical trajectories become available. Bind scores, selected versions, actual pre-write states and repair or completion receipts. No new writer or reader requests. Exclude validation and independent tests.
comparison: Also compute unrestricted placement across the two states subject to the same marginal, plus the upper bound on changing only the root probability by +/-2 at fixed native conditional suffix decisions. The root bound allows a different activity use and is only a diagnostic of where an effective intervention could occur. Report interaction heterogeneity and verified effects from the original factorial rather than inferring selection credit from signs.
